title: Science teacher acts out a man being struck by lightning
note: Gaunt, looming Mr. Rzykruski shouts 'Boom!' and mimes electrocution; the class gasps. Illustrative, nobody is in danger. Mild; least sure this belongs at all.

title: CONTROL (hard): Weird Girl's omen - past accidents retold
note: Deliberately hard. Weird Girl recounts Mr. Whiskers' dreams: Bob 'fell in a manhole', Nassor 'got knocked unconscious' (brief comic flashbacks). Retold, deadpan, nobody in danger now. She is odd-looking but Victor does not react with fear.

title: Sparky chases the ball into the street and is hit by a car
note: Impact is off-screen: '(CAR APPROACHING)', '(THUDDING)', Victor cries 'Sparky! No!'. The death itself is not stated inside the range (only confirmed by the grave scene that follows), hence visual_only for the death attributes. loved_one_dies: Sparky is Victor's only friend.

title: Sparky's grave; parents comfort a grieving Victor; he cries in bed
note: Pet cemetery in the rain, then bedside talk: 'I don't want him in my heart. I want him here with me.' Victor sniffling alone. Deep, realistic pet-loss grief.

title: Dead frog made to kick with electricity in class
note: A dead frog's legs jerk when shocked; students exclaim in disgust. corpses_undead read literally (a dead animal body shown to characters). Mild.

title: Victor digs up Sparky's body in the pet cemetery at night
note: Almost wordless: grunting while digging at night among gravestones, then Mr. Whiskers hisses and Victor gasps. The exhumation itself is invisible to text.

title: Attic laboratory: stitched corpse of Sparky raised into the lightning storm
note: Nearly wordless Frankenstein sequence (22:42-26:00): the sewn-up dead dog with neck bolts is hoisted through the roof into a thunderstorm; loud thunder and electricity. Text shows only thunder/buzzing. Considered dangerous_act (kites in a lightning storm) but no adult forbade it and it is not a dare, so no.

title: Victor thinks it failed and mourns over Sparky's body
note: 'I'm sorry, boy.' Victor hugs the lifeless body in despair, until Sparky's tail wags. The joyful 'You're alive!' that follows is not flagged.

title: CONTROL: breakfast, waffle iron and the 'robotic bucket'
note: Light comic domestic scene; Victor hides Sparky under a bucket and tells him to stay. No danger or distress.

title: Stitched-up Sparky startles a neighbour, who screams
note: Sparky out in the neighbourhood; a neighbour hears growling, sees the undead dog and screams. Comic and brief. Not certain which neighbour (I believe Bob's mother).

title: Bob's soda-rocket jetpack launch off the roof ends in a crash
note: Toshiaki pressures a reluctant Bob into a rooftop launch (read as a dare); Bob flies, crashes, groans in pain, his mother screams, ambulance siren. He later has a broken arm. Comic tone, but a copyable stunt with a real injury. terrified is borderline (mother's scream).

title: CONTROL: Victor talks with Mr. Rzykruski as he leaves
note: Calm, warm conversation about science and doing things for the right reason. Nothing to flag.

title: Parents discover undead Sparky; mother screams; Sparky bolts
note: Dad finds Sparky in the attic, Sparky runs into Mom who screams; the frightened dog whimpers and flees the house while Victor shouts 'Sparky, come back!'. animal_in_danger is borderline (Sparky crying out in fear, not hurt).

title: Parents confront Victor: 'Reanimating a corpse!' - Victor pleads
note: Dad is stern and upset rather than raging (so not adult_rages_at_child). Victor pleads to go after his runaway dog: 'I just wanted my dog back.' Mild; parents turn supportive right after. Unsure this needs flagging.

title: CONTROL (hard-ish): Dutch Day stage, Elsa's song
note: Mayor introduces Elsa, who sings with lit candles on her head. 'I don't think this is safe', 'a lot of girls would kill to be in your place' / 'I'd welcome death' are deadpan jokes; nobody is in danger.

title: Classmates rob pet graves at night; Nassor at the tomb of Colossus
note: Kids enter the pet cemetery in a storm and dig up dead pets for their experiments (intercut with Elsa's song). 'Soon you shall be awakened', evil laughter, thunder. The wordless experiment set-ups run on to about 59:35.

title: Mr. Whiskers bites the dead bat as lightning strikes and mutates into a vampire cat
note: Body-horror transformation of a familiar pet: yowling, gurgling, bones cracking in shadow, then a fanged winged cat hisses at Weird Girl ('Mr. Whiskers?'). C0740 (exclaim in surprise) is probably Edgar's dead rat turning into the were-rat, intercut. Exact attribution of C0740/C0747 to characters is uncertain.

title: Bob alone by the pool: 'Is someone there?' - Sea-Monkeys attack
note: Gremlin-like Sea-Monkeys burst out at a child at night; growling then screaming.

title: Nassor raises Colossus from the tomb
note: Mausoleum at night, thudding footsteps build dread, then the payoff is a tiny mummified hamster (comic). Mild.

title: Toshiaki's turtle Shelley returns as a giant roaring monster
note: 'Shelley?' - then a Gamera-sized turtle looms over the boys, who gasp fearfully; roaring.

title: A boy is chased by his monster through the dark streets
note: Heavy breathing, fearful cries, scream. I believe this is Edgar fleeing the were-rat; character attribution not certain from memory. C0764 (gleeful roars) just before is the Sea-Monkeys reaching the fair.

title: Giant Shelley's footsteps interrupt the boys asking Victor for help
note: The lines before this are retelling ('Did you see those things?') and are not flagged; only the thundering footsteps and roar as the giant turtle looms over town. Brief.

title: Monsters attack the Dutch Day fair; crowd panics
note: Giant turtle stomps into the fair, Sea-Monkeys swarm, townspeople scream and flee; 'No! Get away!', 'This way! In here!'; Victor's mother screams as creatures besiege the parents. war_mass_violence read literally ('an attack on many people at once'); a parent may prefer to drop it. Sustained 100 s of screaming.

title: Nassor orders 'Kill!' - Shelley squashes Colossus
note: Nassor sets his undead hamster on the giant turtle with 'Kill! Kill!'; the hamster is stomped flat ('(SQUISHING)', 'Colossus?'). Played for a laugh. pet_animal_dies/dies_now are debatable because the hamster was already undead.

title: Nassor is wrapped up and sealed in; another child screams 'Get away from me!'
note: Nassor ends up bound like a mummy and shut inside a casket-like prop (muffled cries). Then a child backs away from a growling creature, screaming. From memory I cannot be sure which child says 'Get away from me!' (Edgar with the were-rat, I think).

title: Victor and the boys lure the Sea-Monkeys, which burst after eating salt
note: 'Hey! Over here!' - the swarm chases the boys, gorges on salted snacks and explodes into goo. Bounded by the nearest cues; the popping is wordless, ending at 'Cool.' (C0852).

title: Were-rat attacks Edgar; Sparky fights it; Elsa cornered by the vampire cat
note: Edgar screams, Elsa cries 'Help! Get back! Stay away from us!', Sparky whimpers as the were-rat throws him about; Victor shouts 'Sparky!'.

title: Giant Shelley grabs Toshiaki; Victor electrocutes the monsters
note: 'No, no, no! You put me down! I gave you life!', 'Victor, I need help. Please!' Shelley and the were-rat are shocked with a live power line and revert to small dead animals ('Shelley?'). Considered fall_from_height (held high up) but he is not falling.

title: Vampire cat snatches Persephone and carries Elsa off to the windmill
note: 'No! Persephone! Bring her back!' The winged cat flies off with the poodle and then Elsa (her wig falls off). child_taken is a literal-reading stretch: a child carried off by a monster, from her guardian uncle who is not present.

title: Mob turns on Sparky: 'He's killed the little girl! Kill the monster!'
note: Mayor finds Sparky with Elsa's wig and concludes his niece is dead; torch-bearing mob sets off after the dog.

title: Elsa trapped in the windmill with the vampire cat while the mob hunts Sparky
note: 'Help! Stay away from us!' intercut with 'Get him!' and Sparky whining as he is chased up the hill.

title: Windmill catches fire with Elsa inside
note: The mayor's torch ignites the windmill: 'Look out! It's on fire!', 'There's Elsa!', 'Help!', screaming. Victor and Sparky run in.

title: Elsa dangles from the burning windmill: 'I can't hold on much longer'
note: Child hanging high up while the cat attacks and the mill burns; she slips and screams before being caught.

title: Victor trapped in the burning windmill; 'That's my son in there!'
note: Sparky fights the vampire cat; Victor falls and lies knocked out inside the collapsing mill; firefighters hold his parents back.

title: Mother sobs until Sparky drags Victor out of the fire
note: Parents weep fearing for Victor; Sparky pulls him out limp; 'Honey, are you all right?'. Considered believed_dead but the lines only show fear, not belief.

title: Vampire cat drags Sparky back in; cat is impaled; windmill collapses on Sparky
note: Almost all sound captions: yowls, hisses, whimpers, a screech as a burning beam spears the cat, Sparky's last whimper, then Victor's 'No!' as the mill falls. Sparky's second death; the emotional peak of the film.

title: Sparky's body carried out; Victor grieves
note: Wordless stretch from about 01:16:40 (fireman carries the limp body out and lays it down) belongs here; bounded by the nearest cues. 'You said that I need to let him go.'

title: Townspeople try to jump-start Sparky's body with car batteries
note: Cables clipped to the dead dog's bolts; engines rev, nothing happens. The lines alone read like a car scene.

title: Victor says goodbye: 'You don't have to come back'
note: Victor gives up hope and hugs the body. Followed by a wordless half minute before Sparky revives (C0958-C0960), which is not flagged.

title: CONTROL: end-credits song 'Strange Love'
note: Lyrics only ('The lightning's not frightening when you are with me'). Nothing happening.
